actions: Check engine oil level and correct viscosity/spec first.
If it’s cold-start only and fades within 30–90s, monitor for a few days and avoid hard revs while cold.
If it persists longer than ~2 minutes or worsens, verify oil pressure and inspect for restriction (filter/galley).
stop_now_if: Oil pressure warning light appears or the tick becomes suddenly loud with power loss.
Noise becomes constant even when fully warm.
ignore_risk: Can progress to accelerated valvetrain wear and rough running.

actions: Confirm pattern: brief 1–3s rattle on cold start then gone is classic tensioner behavior.
Reduce repeated short start/stop cycles temporarily (they repeat the same chain slap).
If the rattle gets longer/louder, inspect tensioner and guides before timing jumps.
stop_now_if: Rattle becomes sustained or appears with misfire, rough running, or check engine light.
Harsh rattle under acceleration that instantly quiets on lift-off.
ignore_risk: Chain slack can worsen and potentially jump timing, causing major internal damage.

actions: Track whether it’s only cold and disappears quickly when warm.
Use correct oil spec and a quality filter (oil pressure stability matters).
If it evolves, inspect tensioner/guides and oil control path.
stop_now_if: Noise starts lasting longer or appears when warm.
ignore_risk: May slowly progress into guide wear and severe timing noise.

actions: Test: is it loudest on decel/lift-off or during load transitions? That fits guide wear.
Avoid high RPM and hard kickdown until inspected.
Inspect guides and tensioner promptly.
stop_now_if: Rattle becomes violent with power loss, misfire, or check engine light.
ignore_risk: High risk of timing jump and valve/piston damage depending on engine design.

actions: Test: appears under load and quiets immediately when you lift? Consider phaser control/knock separation.
Verify oil level/quality (VVT is oil-pressure dependent).
If timing-related codes exist, inspect VVT solenoid and phaser operation.
stop_now_if: Strong vibration/roughness with metallic noise under load.
ignore_risk: Can worsen into persistent timing noise and poor performance.

actions: If symptoms started after an oil service, confirm correct oil spec and level.
Pull trouble codes if a light is on—this is a shortcut to the real cause.
Inspect VVT solenoids/oil control and verify actual cam timing.
stop_now_if: Severe misfire/limp mode behavior under throttle.
ignore_risk: Ongoing timing instability increases stress, fuel use, and drivability issues.

actions: Confirm it’s a light, even tick that cleanly follows RPM with no performance symptoms.
Listen near injectors: direct-injection engines often tick normally.
If misfire/roughness appears, shift to ignition/fuel diagnosis.
ignore_risk: Usually harmless when no other symptoms exist.

actions: Localize: top of engine vs front accessory drive.
In Park/Neutral, hold 1500 RPM—if it tracks RPM, it’s valvetrain/accessory related.
If it gets harsher or louder, inspect rocker/lifter/valve lash path.
stop_now_if: Harsh mechanical tap with power loss or strong shake.
ignore_risk: Can progress into mechanical wear and misfire if severe.

actions: Track heat relation: if it fades warm, it’s often minor.
Confirm correct oil spec and filter quality.
If it grows over time, inspect valvetrain components.
stop_now_if: Tick becomes loud with clear misfire/rough running.
ignore_risk: Often low risk, but long neglect can accelerate wear.

actions: Do not continue driving if it’s grinding/hammering—treat as urgent mechanical contact risk.
Check oil level immediately.
Tow for inspection (valvetrain or internal contact possible).
stop_now_if: Any sustained grinding/hammering noise.
ignore_risk: Rapid internal engine damage.

actions: Cold start: sharp tick near manifold that changes as it warms fits a small leak.
Look for soot marks around manifold/joints.
Repair gasket/fasteners before it spreads.
ignore_risk: Usually noise/efficiency issue; can worsen and affect sensors over time.

actions: Warm-only tick suggests a crack/joint opening with thermal expansion.
Inspect for soot at cracks and joints.
Repair before the crack grows.
ignore_risk: Can expand into larger leak and drivability/sensor issues.

actions: If it’s louder on acceleration and quieter on coast, exhaust pressure leak is likely.
Inspect manifold/downpipe joints and flex section.
Repair to prevent expansion.
ignore_risk: Leak may grow and become louder; can impact mixture readings.

actions: With engine cool, lightly press/tap the shield area to reproduce the buzz.
Replace missing clips/fasteners.
Ensure no contact with the exhaust.
ignore_risk: Mostly nuisance, can worsen and vibrate into contact.

actions: If it rattles on bumps/load changes, inspect hangers and rubber mounts.
Confirm the exhaust isn’t hitting the body/subframe.
Replace worn hangers/mounts.
stop_now_if: Exhaust is dragging or striking the body hard.
ignore_risk: Can crack pipes/welds and create leaks.

actions: Hold RPM at the noise range while parked—if it happens, it’s exhaust/body resonance.
Inspect muffler/resonator for internal baffle failure.
Replace the resonator/muffler if confirmed.
ignore_risk: Usually noise; severe internal collapse can restrict flow in rare cases.

actions: If it appears only with speed/wind, inspect undertray/fasteners immediately.
Secure loose edges so they can’t flap into tires.
Replace missing clips/screws.
stop_now_if: Panel is hanging low or contacting tires.
ignore_risk: Can detach and cause damage or a driving hazard.

actions: Do not keep driving—this is metal-to-rotor grinding.
Avoid repeated braking; let the brakes cool.
Replace pads immediately and likely rotors; inspect caliper condition.
stop_now_if: Any grinding during braking.
ignore_risk: Rotor destruction, caliper damage, and dangerous braking loss.

actions: Perform a gentle lane-change test: noise changes with load shift = bearing likely.
After a short drive, carefully compare hub temperature side-to-side.
Plan bearing replacement before it progresses.
stop_now_if: Hum becomes grinding, strong vibration appears, or wheel feels loose.
ignore_risk: Can progress to failure and loss of control risk.

actions: Stop safely immediately.
Check lug nut tightness with the proper tool.
If you can’t verify tightness, tow the vehicle.
stop_now_if: Any suspicion of wheel looseness.
ignore_risk: Wheel can detach.

actions: If squeal lasts a few seconds on cold start, inspect belt and tensioner condition.
Increase electrical load (lights/defrost): if squeal worsens, slip is likely.
Replace belt and/or tensioner as needed.
stop_now_if: Battery light/overheat warning appears or steering assist suddenly changes (if belt-driven).
ignore_risk: Belt can fail and take down charging/cooling/assist systems depending on vehicle.

actions: Add electrical load: if whine changes, alternator involvement increases.
Watch for charging warnings or voltage instability.
Inspect/replace alternator before failure.
stop_now_if: Grinding + battery warning or severe electrical instability.
ignore_risk: Charging failure can strand the vehicle.

actions: Toggle A/C: if noise changes, compressor/clutch path is likely.
If grinding begins, avoid using A/C to reduce load until inspected.
Inspect compressor bearing/clutch before it seizes and throws the belt.
stop_now_if: Strong grinding or belt distress noises.
ignore_risk: Compressor seizure can damage the belt drive and cause loss of systems.

actions: If hiss at idle + rough/lean symptoms, suspect unmetered air leak.
Inspect vacuum hoses, PCV lines, and intake ducting.
If lean codes exist, fix leaks first before chasing sensors.
ignore_risk: Lean running can overheat combustion and worsen drivability.

actions: At idle, press the brake pedal: if RPM changes and hiss increases, booster leak is likely.
If brake feel changes (hard pedal/weak assist), treat as urgent.
Inspect booster and check valve immediately.
stop_now_if: Brake assist becomes weak or pedal becomes abnormally hard.
ignore_risk: Direct braking safety risk.

actions: Reduce throttle immediately—do not load the engine while pinging.
If available, test one tank of higher octane only as a diagnostic hint (not a permanent fix).
Investigate root causes: heat, lean condition, ignition, VVT, carbon buildup.
stop_now_if: Knock becomes harsh with power loss even at light throttle.
ignore_risk: Severe knock can damage pistons/valves over time, rapidly if intense.

actions: Do not drive—deep knock under load suggests bottom-end damage risk.
Check oil level immediately.
Tow for oil pressure verification and bearing inspection.
stop_now_if: Any deep knock that worsens with throttle.
ignore_risk: Catastrophic engine failure (thrown rod) is possible.

actions: If it’s cold-only and disappears warm, keep revs low until warmed up.
Avoid hard acceleration when cold.
If it starts occurring when warm, reassess diagnosis.
ignore_risk: Often moderate; persistent warm knock needs re-evaluation.

actions: Do the two isolation checks: rev in Park/Neutral (RPM relation) and steady-speed test (speed relation).
Report whether it is cold-only or warm-only.
Report whether it is worse under load or on coast.
ignore_risk: Without relation data, multiple causes overlap and diagnosis becomes guesswork.

actions: Record 10s at idle and 10s at ~1500 RPM near the source.
Confirm: does it follow RPM while parked or only road speed?
Confirm: cold-only, warm-only, or both?
ignore_risk: Overlapping causes without relation tests.

actions: Engine test: does the same sound appear while stationary when you raise RPM?
Wheel test: does the sound change during a gentle lane shift at the same speed?
Once separated, the diagnosis becomes high-confidence.
ignore_risk: Wrong path wastes time and can miss safety issues.
